conventions.convention: Allowed paths are one-sided DQM paths with a common sigma-finite dominator; derivatives are right derivatives. The tangent space is the closed real linear span of allowed scores, rather than the tangent set itself.

Parameter influence curves represent continuous path derivatives; estimator influence functions describe empirical-average expansions. Neither notion alone asserts local regularity or estimator attainment.
Influence curves and scores are real mean-zero L²(P) classes modulo P-almost-sure equality; vector formulas and projections operate coordinatewise.
Countable Choice supplies Hilbert projection and Riesz representation. The separate Axiom-of-Choice convention supplies selected density versions along general dominated paths.

Efficient information is a second-moment matrix and need not be nonsingular. Its inverse gives the canonical gradient only under the theorem's exact allowed-score decomposition, target-derivative convention, and nonsingularity hypothesis.
The mean examples designate only paths dP(t,s)=(1+ts)dP with bounded centered scores and sufficiently small t≥0.

load_bearing.statement: Let H be a real Hilbert space, T a closed linear subspace, and dotψ:T→Rᵏ continuous linear with an ambient representer φ₀∈Hᵏ. Assume Countable Choice. All ambient representers are exactly φ₀+(T⊥)ᵏ, and the unique representer in Tᵏ is the coordinatewise projection Π_Tφ₀.

Pathwise differentiability requires the right derivative to exist for every allowed path, depend only on its score, and extend to a continuous linear map on the closed tangent space. A parameter influence curve φ∈L²₀(P)ᵏ represents that map by dotψ_P(s)=E_P[φs]; its unique representer in the tangent space is the canonical gradient under Countable Choice.

For a finite interest-score vector Sθ∈L²₀(P)ᵖ and a closed nuisance tangent space Tη, define S_eff=Sθ−Π_TηSθ and I_eff=E_P[S_eff S_effᵀ], with projection applied coordinatewise. Nonsingularity is not asserted.

A measurable estimator sequence is asymptotically linear at P with estimator influence function φ∈L²₀(P)ᵏ if its error is (P_n−P)φ+o_P(n⁻¹ᐟ²). This definition alone does not assert local regularity, pathwise differentiability, or asymptotic normality.

Assume AC and Countable Choice, closed nuisance and full tangent spaces Tη⊆T⊆L²₀(P), and an interest-score vector Sθ. Suppose the allowed score set is exactly {aᵀSθ+t:a∈Rᵖ,t∈Tη}, T is its closure, and every allowed path with that score has right target derivative a. If I_eff is nonsingular, the target is pathwise differentiable with canonical gradient I_eff⁻¹S_eff and covariance I_eff⁻¹.

seams_checked.note: The DQM, score-centering, tangent-set, closed-span, mean-zero Hilbert, and nuisance-space suppliers agree with the consuming definitions. One-sided paths, almost-sure classes, and choice assumptions are preserved.

The score definition supplies log-density derivatives and second-moment information. The efficient-score definition separately assumes Sθ∈L²₀(P), rather than inferring centering or integrability from differentiability alone.

This is contextual prerequisite material; no assigned proof imports an LAN, convolution, or minimax conclusion. The opened interior-vector QMD definition restricts along θ₀+tv to the stated one-sided scalar DQM convention. The assigned page explicitly disclaims estimator attainment.

The opened asymptotic-normality, regular-AL information-bound, and general convolution-bound items use the exact estimator expansion, continuous tangent derivative, and affine representer class. Regularity is imposed separately, and AC/Countable Choice are retained where the representation conclusions are used.

The statistical-functional definition accurately distinguishes pointwise gross-error derivatives from parameter influence curves and estimator influence functions. It does not assume contamination paths are allowed DQM paths or import the choice-dependent representation conclusions.
